scope: Final visible Draft; exact source/article/action/deployed bytes; core #510/#622-#629 and pinned #627 map; daily-logger #555-#577 and pinned #566 plan; core #625/#626; exact packaging workflow/scripts; public rendering; all-state same-source review searches; current review schema/discovery; and held-candidate custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The service-slice counts and composition conflict
findings.location: Lines 3, 6, 11, 57, 59 and 73 say fifteen new service Drafts, then say nineteen simultaneous Drafts include prior #555 and review-data PR #558.
findings.explanation: PRs #559-#577 are nineteen service Drafts created before the cutoff. Prior service Drafts #555 and #556 make twenty-one service Drafts. PR #558 is an independent review-data record, not a service slice.
findings.correction: Report nineteen new service Drafts and twenty-one open service Drafts when #555/#556 are included; keep review-data PR #558 outside the service-stack count.

findings.title: Docker did not rerun the 33 proof tests
findings.location: Lines 17 and 53 say the Docker clean-consumer build installs the tarball and reruns the full 33-test suite plus bin invocations.
findings.explanation: Core #629 separates the required proof:local:test CI step from Docker packaging. The Dockerfile builds, packs, installs and imports the tarball; the packaging script runs package checks, negative probes and a synthetic lifecycle, not the 33 node:test cases.
findings.correction: Distinguish the required 33-test source/CI step from the Docker package/install and synthetic lifecycle proof; do not say Docker reran the 33 tests.

findings.title: Core #627 already records the M3 hold and next decision
findings.location: Lines 71, 83 and 84 say the M3 unblocking action is absent and propose extracting it from core #627.
findings.explanation: Core #627 head fc5f01e was recorded before article capture and names the signed-readiness practice, teardown HELD result, generic terminal error, owners, required teardown/native-terminal resolution and next owner decision.
findings.correction: Report the recorded M3 hold, owners, retired practice ID and next owner decision; do not create a duplicate extraction task.

findings.title: The service plan contradicts the claimed unblocked slices
findings.location: Lines 59, 73, 83 and 84 say the order was not fully visible, call #559/#567 independently unblocked and propose extracting the sequence from #566.
findings.explanation: The pinned #566 roadmap already had its dependency table and current qualification sequence. PR #559 depends on #555; PR #567 is stacked on #564.
findings.correction: Use #566's existing sequence and the PR dependency records; do not call #559/#567 independently unblocked or propose duplicate extraction work.

findings.title: PR #571 proves inactive packaging, not trace delivery
findings.location: Lines 65 and 84 say #571 is the first nominal or happy-path Langfuse delivery qualification.
findings.explanation: PR #571 requires disabled telemetry and zero batches. #573/#574 later qualify enabled transport only against a synthetic receiver. All leave real Langfuse ingestion/readback, capacity and retention open.
findings.correction: Describe #571 as inactive/default-off packaging, #573/#574 as synthetic enabled transport, and actual Langfuse readback as unqualified.

findings.title: PR #563 is offline mapping, not live LangSmith evidence
findings.location: Lines 73 and 84 call #563 the first live evidence or vendor-lock-in event for the LangSmith selection.
findings.explanation: PR #563 adds no endpoint, credentials, ambient resource, baggage or network configuration and does not qualify LangSmith ingestion/readback, region, overhead, recovery, retention or evaluation quality.
findings.correction: Describe #563 as bounded offline OTel mapping; reserve live-evidence language for authenticated LangSmith readback and qualification.

findings.title: Core #510 already records rationale, alternatives and gates
findings.location: Lines 73, 83 and 84 say alternatives and written rationale are absent and propose a new LangSmith-selection ADR.
findings.explanation: Core #510 records the operator selection, historic alternatives, OTel portability boundary, resource-cost measures, qualification gates, privacy/recovery requirements and unresolved thresholds.
findings.correction: Point to #510 and state which measured values remain unknown; amend or consume that decision record instead of presenting its rationale as absent or duplicating it.

findings.title: Core #626 has acceptance criteria through issue #625
findings.location: Line 71 says #626 has no recorded acceptance criteria while separately noting active issue #625.
findings.explanation: PR #626 tracks issue #625. The issue defines ordered decision reviews, retained invariants, required sources and a first review checkpoint with a concrete target-repo setup contract.
findings.correction: Report #626 as the roadmap link for #625's explicit checklist and first checkpoint; separate missing assignee from missing acceptance criteria.

findings.title: The asserted second-person review is not attributable
findings.location: Line 71 defines independent review as a second-person review and treats M2 as complete through packaging.
findings.explanation: Core #629 says M2 required independent reviews, but its public history has no submitted reviews and only an automated skill-audit comment. #627 reports an exact-head review without naming its reviewer or exposing the receipt. Shared-account publication does not authenticate a second person, human, provider or machine.
findings.correction: Retain packaging and merge evidence, but identify the review receipt and reviewer basis or leave independence and second-person identity unverified; keep human merge authority separate.
